messages.author: ed37958eb3ca2b8c
messages.subject: "threads" argument in occu
parts:
Hi,

I am fitting single-season occupancy models using occu to some large data sets and noticed the function is using a large number of "threads" when fitting which I don't always want it to. I would like to be able to set the number of threads manually but the threads argument in occu doesn't seem to be working for me. I am not sure whether this is limited to occu... for example I tried changing the threads argument for occuRN using just the simple example from the help file and it seems to work, whereas for occu it doesn't (again including just running the example in the help file). For the moment I have set the argument engine="R", but ideally I would prefer to use the faster C++ option. 

Help/advice with this would be much appreciated,
Emily

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: "threads" argument in occu
parts:
Hi Emily,

unmarked uses the Armadillo C++ library for linear algebra via RcppArmadillo. It seems that when you have very large datasets (and thus large model matrices etc.), Armadillo or perhaps one of its underlying libraries automatically does some computations in parallel if you have openMP support on your computer. I have also noticed this for occuMulti. So far I have not found a way to disable this from inside or outside R, despite trying setting various environmental variables, so I am not sure if there is much we can do about it at this point short of not using RcppArmadillo. If anyone on the list has figured out how to change this I would be very interested.

You're correct that the threads argument in occu() doesn't do anything at the moment. I was planning to add some parallel computation functionality to occu at some point, but didn't (partially because of the issue you have), so the argument needs to be removed. It does currently work on some other functions as you noted such as occuRN.  

Can you try running the model with engine="TMB" assuming you are on an up-to-date unmarked? The TMB engine should be similarly fast but uses RcppEigen instead of RcppArmadillo, and based on my tests, does not seem to try to use more than one thread.

Ken
